utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We had a late start this morning because of the need for some dental treatment to one of the accused. If I could remind you, Mr. Bushi, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that all members of the NLA had to wear uniforms. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness may please be shown 65 ter 2D00-207.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you recognise the person in the middle of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only him, I can recognise all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is the person in the middle of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the court usher please assist the witness to mark Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you circle Mr. Ali Ahmeti, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmeti, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And mark him with the number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person with the beard, to the left of him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please mark him with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the name of Commander Hoxha is Xhezairi Selajdin?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D54, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court Usher, can the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter 2D00-208.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see Ali Ahmeti on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark him with the number 5?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The person kneeling to the utmost left with the number 6 on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on this picture none of the persons are wearing ranks?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot see the ranks here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, you had a person marked with a number 6. Do you want that person identified?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would not want this person to be identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can you please explain to me how this person is dressed?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The person marked as number 6. Is this correct that he is dressed in a green T-shirt, pants, and sneakers?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see his footwear. I see the T-shirt, it was part of the uniform. I see that he is wearing a head gear with the NLA insignia. And his trousers here are either black or dark blue. We didn't have dark blue uniforms, but we did have black uniforms. But this picture might have been taken during a free time, when the soldiers could sit around and rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If the person number 6 were to be stripped of his head wear he would be left with a Kalashnikov and he would not be resembling a member of the NLA but a civilian with a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that, because the T-shirt is part of the uniform. To what I can see here on the picture, everyone is wearing something that identifies him as member of the NLA. The head gear, the uniforms, the T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be -- yes, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Could we have the date when this photo was taken and also the previous photo, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that the witness confirmed yesterday that the markings of the NLA are worn from the formation of the NLA until its disarmament, this photograph would have taken from the period of February to September 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you don't have available to you the date where either of these photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. By the markings and the evidence of witness it should be a period from February to September 2001. In fact, it was confirmed that the person on the photograph was Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about the location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're wanting to know the location, are you. Are you able to assist with that, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that the witness confirmed that the NLA was on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, the precise location is unknown, but nonetheless it is on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You don't know the location either. Is that what you're saying? The witness may be able to help you with either location or date, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, can you perhaps identify the location of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the first photograph or on both of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm now asking you about this photograph.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the people that I see on the photograph, it should be in the Tetovo area, in the Shar mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you identify perhaps the time when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That I cannot do. I don't know the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At any rate, you can confirm that this is a period between February and September 2001.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should know that, if you have it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does your answer mean that you know and confirm that, or that you don't know when the photograph is dated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, sir, when the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in respect of the other photograph, are you able to give any identification of the location or the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're referring to the first photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can say the location. It is in the premises of the General Staff in the village of Sipkovica in Tetovo area, but I cannot say anything about the time when it was taken. It is taken in the work office of the commander, Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Regue, is there anything further?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we won't object. But just for the record that the time-frame has not been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. The second photograph will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D55, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter 2D00-209.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the area where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the exact location, but I can identify the general area, because I see some people on the photograph and I know in which area they were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In which area did they operate?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in the area of Tetovo, in the Shar mountain. In Tetovo area, Shar mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we see green grass in the background, is it right to say that this is a period of spring and summer of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot pinpoint the exact time. I can assist you with identifying the persons that I recognise on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you mark Ali Ahmeti with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person that is kneeling in front of Mr. Ali Ahmeti dressed in black?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please mark this person with the number 7.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me what he is wearing and whether he has the insignia of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- part of the uniform, the black uniform of the special unit. I can see his full black uniforms. There should be a jacket that is part of this black uniform, and the insignia, the NLA insignia, is on the jacket. And that would make the set of uniform complete. This is the black uniform. It is the black trousers, black shirt and the black footwear.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You could, in any event, agree with me that these are summer uniforms, because they're all wearing T-shirts. Did you have just winter uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not necessarily mean that it is a summer uniform. But as for the second part of your question, we didn't have winter one. Sir, you should be familiar with the fact that in every regular army and from my experience in the former Yugoslav army and in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, you wear civilian clothes during free time, and this goes also for the NLA. During free time when soldiers were having rest, they were allowed to be dressed in training suits.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In track suits, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on any of these persons, do you see any of these persons wearing a rank?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I can see, Dreni has it on front. But I'm not completely precise. It resembles a rank to me, but maybe it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the rank please be marked with an X?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: One more question. The free time which you were talking about, which the soldiers used, do they spend their free time with arms, weapons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During free time, of course they had their weapons always with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So in their free time, they were members of the organisation NLA, were dressed in civilian clothing, and throughout the whole time they had their weapons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The light weapons, the pistols and the Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, not the Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that each member of the NLA had a pistol as formation weapons, in addition to the Kalashnikovs?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct that each and every soldier had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us from a formation point of view, which -- who had to carry a pistol?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders, starting from the brigade commander, down to the platoon commander, but it was possible also for the soldiers to wear them. It was not prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D56, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You recognise the General Staff of Ali Ahmeti of the NLA organisation, can you tell us when this was moved to Sipkovica?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Approximately the month, which month it was moved?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter number 2D00-212.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see Ali Ahmeti, and could you please circle him and mark him with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us or to recognise the location where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you identify the time when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on this photograph members of the NLA, some dressed in uniforms and others in jeans and T-shirts in the formation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, but this could have -- this photograph could have been taken during the mobilisation of the soldiers during a tour that Mr. Ali Ahmeti made of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Why are, then, some of them dressed in uniforms and some in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on which particular moment they arrived there. Maybe they had just arrived and came there to get mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since yesterday you gave evidence that once people joined the NLA, members of the NLA were issued uniforms. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This could be the moment when they arrived there. We don't know the time when they were photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We seek to tender this exhibit into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D57, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the photograph number 2D00-213. I apologise, can the photograph 2D00-214, 65 ter be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you -- could you please show me in this photograph or could you explain what is the territory where the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where it was taken. I can only say it is not part of Karadak.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you describe what was the time-period?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that the -- some of the NLA terrorists are wearing uniforms and some are wearing T-shirts and jeans in this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly you mean soldiers who are not terrorists. Some are in uniform, some are not, but, as I said -- I have to answer the question you asked me. It was a mobilisation time which went on until the end of July when the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D58, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown number 2D00-218.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you please encircle Mr. Ali Ahmeti and mark it with a number 5; and the person who is two men away from him to the left wearing black head gear, could you please mark him with a number 6?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Wearing green T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, could you recognise the location of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you where it was taken. I don't recognise all the persons here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please indicate what was the time when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. I don't know when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D59, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph 65 ter number 2D00-219.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please encircle the person wearing black trousers, black T-shirt and black head gear and could you mark him with a number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, green T-shirt, not black T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He is in the middle of the picture in the front row.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please confirm that everyone else is wearing T-shirts and jeans, all the people behind him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. Some of them. Some are with complete uniforms, but the T-shirt is also part of the uniform because, as you see, they are wearing black trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but some of them are wearing blue jeans?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D60, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph 65 ter number 2D00-220.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell us perhaps where was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The person with the black head gear, second from the left, and in the middle row, could you please mark him with a number 6; the one next to him the first one from the left, the first one in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The one next to him, the first one in the photograph, could you please mark him with a number 7.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the same row, the first person from the right-hand side, could you please mark that with number 8.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The one at the extreme right, in the middle row, could you mark him with the number 9, wearing green T-shirt and jeans.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how is the person marked with the number 7 dressed?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person with number 7 is dressed in T-shirt, which is part of the uniform, with boots, and with a track suit, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please describe the person marked with the number 9. What is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A training suit and a T-shirt which is part of the uniform, a green T-shirt. And, in fact, in jeans.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please also mark the person kneeling to the right in the bottom row, could you please mark him with a number 10.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A T-shirt, part of the uniform, and I can't see very well what he is wearing underneath. I think he is wearing jeans.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are the persons marked with the numbers 7, 9 and 10 and 8, do they wear any NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have the T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are they wearing any patches?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. They -- [Indiscernible] something that goes on top -- has the insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And if those person would not be together with the others, would they look like civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can identify them on the basis of the T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the second microphone of the witness be turned off because there is a lot of noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is your answer, yes, they look like civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Since they are wearing part of the uniforms, no. I said even earlier, even in regular armies, I will -- I would like to answer, sir. Even in regular armies, I served in two armies myself that of the former Yugoslavia and Macedonia, it has happened sometimes that during my free time as an officer I was wearing a track suit. It doesn't mean that have you to wear the uniform all the time. There are moments when you want to take a rest when you are free.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are having difficulties hearing the witness. Could his other microphone be turned off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since these are part of the free time activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You just stated that even in the regular army civilian uniforms were worn. So does it mean that the NLA is not a regular army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying this. My point is this: That this was also a regular army, just like any other regular army would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this photograph be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: With regards to the persons that I asked you about previously in the photograph, if they would be killed, would they look like civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We couldn't pick up the answer, I'm sorry. Can the witness be asked to repeat his last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you give your answer again, please, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now there seems to be a good deal of electrical interference coming from somewhere. It is not apparent where. And it is making it very difficult for the witness, in particular, to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was told that it seems that the noise comes from this lapel microphone that the technicians asked me to use at the beginning of the trial. It seems that this is the thing creating the noise and I will not use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Let's hope that improves things.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter photograph number 2D00-221.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see Xhezairi? And if you do, please mark him with a number 1. And the person sitting first from the right-hand side, could you please mark him with a number 10.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No, please mark with the number 10 the person sitting on the extreme right, not next to Hoxha, but on the extreme right.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise, maybe, the area where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the persons, the superior officers and the soldiers, I can tell you what part of the zone but not the particular place. I think it's in the Shari zone, in the Tetovo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what was the time-period? Could you identify when was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot identify the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D62, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me about the person marked with the number 10. How old is he, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, I couldn't say exactly how old he is. He might be in his 50s, early 50s. Maybe I'm wrong. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what was the commanding officer post of Hoxha?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was the commander of a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the commander Hoxha is directly linked to the Al Qaeda, do you have any such information that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. And if anyone else would assert before this Tribunal that this is correct, then he would be lying, he would not be telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph number 2D00-235.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark Hoxha with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the person to the left of him, could you mark him with the number 12.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me who is the person lying, wearing NLA insignia in the middle of the photograph? Is he the present mayor of Tetovo, Hazbi Lika?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He was for a time commander of 112 Brigade. Then after that he was transferred to the General Staff, and then he -- he was replaced by Ilir Salik [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark him with the number 50.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does any of the persons here wear ranks?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't distinguish them here. Some of them are also wearing something on their chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you recognise whether they were wearing ranks, and could you circle the ranks. Where are they? Could you mark them with an X. If you see them; then if you don't, then you don't need to mark anything.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it clearly, and it's probably the person wearing vests might be wearing ranks, but I can't see it from this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So in these photographs you do not see any person wearing ranks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I seek to tender this photograph into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D63, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show again the 65 ter photograph number 2D00-235, and can we hold it at the screen while at the same time showing the photograph 65 ter number 2D00-236, in order to compare them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the person wearing the uniform in the photograph on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does he look like the person at the photograph to the left, the one holding the Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So could we mark with the number 12 in the photograph on the right-hand side this person?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please describe the person. What is he wearing, the person standing next to him in this photograph and holding a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is wearing dress -- black uniform of the special unit, black trousers and black shirts. On the left side is the NLA logo and the sniper and sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is he wearing sneakers?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. I said he is wearing sneakers, but the remainder is part of the uniform. That is, the trousers, the shirts, the weapon, which is a sniper --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if this person were to be killed, would he look like a civilian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I seek to tender the photograph at the right-hand side of the screen, 65 ter number 2D00-236 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you want to tender it with the marking, you'll either have to have it in combination as it appears on the screen at the moment or we need to delete the left hand photograph and mark the right one again. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In combination, Your Honours, if I may. Both them as they are presently on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 2D64, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we usually took the break at 10.30. Considering that we started at 9.30 today, should we take the break now or should I continue my cross-examination so that we have the usual times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would continue for about another quarter of an hour, Mr. Apostolski. We'll have to adjust our times today.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter 2D00-242. This is a photograph obtained from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on this photograph a small child next to NLA terrorists ready for combat?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are not NLA terrorists; rather, NLA soldiers. The children were proud of these soldiers. Whenever they saw them, they tried to come near them. How can a terrorist have an insignia and a uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this in accordance with the Geneva Conventions to -- for them to be or to act together with children?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You really surprise me with your question. Sir, this is not true. You have just one purpose in mind. Nobody can justify the killing of Erxhan Aliu, the small child and this should be clear to you. Your purpose -- the purpose of your question is this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D65, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 65 ter number 2D00-243. I would skip this photograph. Can we open the photograph 65 ter 2D00-244. Again, this is the wrong photograph. My apologies. 65 ter 2D00-249.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are these indubitably members of the NLA from Macedonia, according to the insignia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you identify the location where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, because I don't know any of these persons in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you perhaps identify the time when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot identify the time either.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the counsel could please wait for the witness to finish his answer because there is overlapping and it is difficult for the interpreters to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see and tell us what the writings on those T-shirts are?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately something like Oxha but I cannot read it clearly. It could be Oxha but it could be not either.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you circle the person with the long hair with the number 15 -- and mark him with the number 15?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your microphone was off, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. And I have been warned by the interpreters and perhaps, as a result of this, they did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please mark the first person to the right with the number 16.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the first person to the left with the number 17.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you describe the person marked with the number 16? Can you explain to us how he is dressed?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what can I see, he is wearing jeans and T-shirt, which is part of the uniform, and he is wearing the NLA insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were jeans part of your uniform?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, they were not part of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a photograph MFI, 1D--

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies Your Honour, for this interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph MFI 1D94. Is it possible to show at the same time photograph 65 ter number 2D00-250 and -- in order to make a comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, if you want these markings it will have to be received as it is first.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- yes, Your Honours, we seek to tender this document into evidence first because I would like to make -- to compare this one with another photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see photograph 65 ter 2D00-249, and, at the same time, photograph 65 ter number 2D00-250, in order to compare them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you able to see the two photographs in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we enlarge somewhat the photograph on the right, the person on the utmost left. Left.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this resemble anyone from the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom out the picture in its regular size?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The third person on the left, does this person resemble any person on the other photograph on the left?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark this on the right photograph with the number 16.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can the person on the utmost left please be marked with the number 15.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us how he is dressed, the person identified with the number 16?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 16 is dressed in jeans and in T-shirt without the insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark the person next to the number 16, the one with the hand raised up high, with the number 17.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this person resemble any of the persons on the left photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. You may say he resembles, but I cannot see him clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps to assist you, does it resemble perhaps the person on the extreme left of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may resemble him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the other persons on this photograph on the right are dressed, the photograph on the right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I can see, they're all civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the person third from -- going from the right to the left holding a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it your evidence also that he, too, is civilian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see at this moment, he looks like a civilian but it is also possible that this group of people came there to join the ranks of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please respond whether this person resembles a civilian to you, a yes and a no -- or a no, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he is wearing civilian clothes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the photograph on the right, do you see a person wearing the insignia of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for number 15. I see the insignia on the chest. I can see a red colour, but I cannot see insignia on the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If these persons were to be attacked by the Macedonian security forces and killed, would they resemble civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, if the person with number 15 was killed, he is an NLA, he has a uniform, the insignia. As for the rest, I would say that they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The presumption that let's say that they were attacked, that the Macedonian security forces attacked this group and the person identified with number 15 succeeded in escaping, would this mean that the other persons who were killed would be civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this document into evidence together, both photographs jointly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned colleague has -- we will object first of all to this request as my learned colleague has not established the time when these two photos were taken, neither the context where these photos were taken. And also he is not able to say whether the other people who are dressed in civilian clothes ever joined the NLA or if they are -- if they were members of the NLA. He cannot speak for the rest of the people. He can only identify a couple of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, together with the previous photograph where we see the same persons wearing a uniform confirmed by the witness, uniforms with the NLA insignia, I link the other photographs because the persons 16 and 17 are identified as well as 15 are identified as members of the NLA. This was done so by the witness. In view of the fact that we're talking about the same persons, I believe that this is relevant evidence that should be received by the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The difficulty, Mr. Apostolski, apart from the person numbered as 15, is that there is no way of knowing which photograph was taken first in time. So it may be that when the photograph on the right-hand side was taken, nobody there was a member of the NLA. You see the problem of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, person -- the person on the right of the photograph, the one with the Kalashnikov, the T-shirt, jeans, and sneakers third from the left confirms that we have in question here an armed persons together in the presence with the person numbered with 15, a member of the NLA. The witness claimed that NLA was disarmed in September, 26th of September. Therefore, this photograph must have been taken prior to 26th of September, in the period between February and 26th of September. Therefore, in view of the fact that the terms of indictment is this time-frame and the case of the Defence is that the NLA was infiltrated together with civilians and that the members of the NLA in civilian clothing went into the villages, I believe that this photographs should be received by this esteemed Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I reiterate that the problem is the time; we don't know when this photo was taken. And the fact that two people resemble on the right photo two people from the left photo and the fact that maybe some of them on the right photo are wearing weapons, that doesn't establish that this photo was taken within the time-period that my learned colleague is mentioning, because we don't know whether these weapons were from the NLA or where they were coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The identification of number 15 appears to the Chamber to offer a sufficient basis for receiving the photograph, but we have already indicated, Mr. Apostolski, that in the absence of any further evidence there appears difficulty in being able to attach any weight to this photograph for other purposes. But it will be received in evidence and we will see whether other evidence does provide any assistance in due course. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D67, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, this is -- I wanted to propose whether this would be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 25 past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honour, if you would allow me to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask to you let me speak about the last photograph so that we all are clear. Two elements are very important that I would like to point out here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be better if the course of the ordinary procedure were followed. It has been noted already, I'm sure, by the Prosecution that you want to say something more about those photographs, and it will be a matter which they can take up. So, Mr. Apostolski, if you would continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, could you agree with me that an attack of a train is a terrorist attack -- the attack of a passenger train is a terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that an attack on a court would be a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that planting dynamite in a church ten centuries old and its destruction is a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've pointed this out earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown a video-clip bis -- 65 ter -- there's no sound. Without a 65 ter and without a sound. Can we please show the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree with me what you have seen just now would be a terrorist act, according to you, and a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't agree with you on -- at this moment. There was combat going on there. There was shelling from all sides. And you should support your claim that we are the ones who carried that out by facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know which church is in question here?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could play it again. I cannot tell you right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the video-clip be shown again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the church now, and do you recognise the church?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be in Matejce. Not necessarily, but it looks to me like it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I shall assist you. Does this perhaps resemble to you the church in the Lesok monastery?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. Maybe. I have not seen the monastery at Lesok.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Lesok monastery was mined and destroyed by the terrorist organisation ONA in 2001, in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a terrorist organisation. It is the National Liberation Army, and it is not true that it was mined by this army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, your evidence before this Chamber is that the Lesok monastery was not destroyed by the NLA in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm saying this with full responsibility. If such a thing had happened in Lesok, a similar thing would have happened in the other monastery which we had in our possession for the entire time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Matejce monastery was under your control?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the upper part of the monastery in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the church and the frescos from the monastery were damaged by members of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which aspect do you mean "damaged"? Could you be more clear on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were they desecrated by markings over them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but not damaged or destroyed. It is possible that there were things written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 2D136, 65 ter 2D236.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this a photograph from the monastery in Matejce?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you say that something was written on the walls, did you have in mind this symbol which you see now over the frescos?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, symbols or other writings, I don't know. But as far as destruction or damage of religious facilities is concerned there weren't such.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to you, is this desecration of a religious facility?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on who is making the comment. I wouldn't say so. You have levelled with earth all the mosques, sir, and we didn't do anything to your churches.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 2D -- 65 ter 2D139.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall that in the monastery of Matejce this fresco was desecrated in this manner?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this, and I don't know which time-frame you're referring to when you mention the monastery in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period during which you were in the monastery. You know that the church is eight centuries old. Do you know of this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know and I will repeat again, sir, that this could have happened even after the demobilisation of the NLA. Do you have any information about the time-period when this was done?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I seek to tender into evidence the photograph 65 ter 2D136, which was identified by the witness that he was aware -- he actually recognised the church where his brigade was located. That would be the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Were you wanting to speak, Ms. Regue, I looked and thought you were --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I wasn't going object, Your Honour. Just wanted to know if he could provide with the time. If ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to help there, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on the photograph itself, one could see an NLA member with a black and red insignia and the witness confirmed that it was worn between March and September. And the witness himself verified that this was the monastery where his brigade was located and the witness himself said that there were graffiti written on the walls. So I think that the Court should receive it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer is you can't give us a date but you would like it to be admitted and it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you something: Were the members of your organisation supposed to carry out their tasks and duties pursuant to the constitution, the Law on Defence and the internal rules?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which constitution and Law on Defence are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time we did not recognise the constitution of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the NLA play a role in the defence of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which UCK are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the NLA, ONA, your organisation, NLA, play a role in the defence of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear on your question, sir. The UCK of Macedonia was formed after the liberation of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the NLA in Macedonia did not play any role in the defence of Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What protection are you talking about? Against whom would the NLA protect Kosova? Please ask the question more clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution was wondering about the relevance of this line of questioning to the present case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you help us with that, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish the witness, since he has been a commander of one of the brigades to confirm whether the NLA infiltrated into Kosovo or was it the other way around: The members of the UCK, KLA from Kosovo came to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What happened in Kosovo doesn't immediately appear to have any bearing upon this case, unless you are able to suggest some connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To say honestly, Your Honour, I need this answer in order to question another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will withdraw the question. I'm withdrawing the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, then, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the NLA in March take down two helicopters, destroyed two tanks and four APCs and has it seized significant quantity of ammunition, are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the real number. I only know that material damage was inflicted on the Macedonian side.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, line 35, 19, armoured vehicles and not APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were two helicopters of the Macedonian security forces taken down?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know the accurate number, but to my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the NLA have the 40th Medicine Battalion -- Medical Battalion?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a battalion, general medical battalion of the NLA, but I don't know the number that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness. I just wish to seek into evidence the video-clip from the press conference of Mr. George Robertson, Secretary-General of NATO and high representative of foreign and security policy of the European Union Javier Solana, the video we watched yesterday and for which we had prepared an English transcript of the entire press conference and it is now in e-court, 65 ter 2D00-384.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, together with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D69, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, I would like to seek to tender into evidence the interview with Mark Dickenson, ambassador of Great Britain in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001 from the end of March. And a transcript of it was made, number 65 ter 2D00-385.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D70, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also seek to tender into evidence the interview with Mark Dickenson, the Great Britain ambassador in Macedonia in 2001, made at the beginning of May 2001. The video-clip as well as the transcript with the number 65 ter 2D00-386.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D71, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions of this witness. I have finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call Exhibit P461 and go to page 1 of the document. The second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, we can see in front of us the regulation on the competencies and work of the brigade command. You were asked by my learned colleague on page 5646 whether you had in your unit an office for public relations and a public information office. Excuse me, can we please turn to the next page, page number 2. Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, being asked these questions by my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You testified that you had an officer for morale and information and also that you had an information centre shared between the 113 and 14th brigade which was located in the Karadak region. If we could have also the Macedonian table of contents. Were these people and was this unit performing the functions that the office for public relations and the office for public information would do, would generally take care of?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their task was to collect all information -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. But my question was basically whether this person that you mentioned, your officer for morale and the information centre that you had in Karadak would be taking care of the functions described in the position of the office for information and public relations and also within the information sector. Would these people and would this centre be taking care of these functions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Such persons had this responsibility. We had a centre for information for Brigade 113 and 14 there were two officers, Brigade 114 had its own officer, Brigade 113 had its own, whereas the centre for information was one. The duty was to collect all the information during the day, to go to the terrain, to tour the army units, and in a way, to help raise the morale of the soldiers, inform them of the current situation and of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. You were also asked about the position of legal advisor that we see in number five of this table of contents and you were also asked about the position of the department for civilian affairs that we see in number 14. And you testified in the negative. If the war would have come -- would have not come to an end, which other positions you would have set up within your brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was awaiting the answer of the witness if he wants to answer this question first, but this is totally speculative. The issue which is relevant is insofar as the structure or the pretended structure of this organ is concerned is what existed at the time relevant to the charges, not at any time after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, this witness testified that he was in the process of establishing the formation of the brigade. So therefore I would like to explore this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want to learn what are the roles of the two positions you've named which were not filled at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to know which other positions was he expecting to create.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you want me to repeat my question, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is clear to me. All the positions that were foreseen on the basis of the military formations and the internal rules were to be created.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now could we please show 65 ter 2D00-367, page 6. This is the statement of Mr. Gezim Ostreni. If we could go to page number 6, paragraph 28. If we could enlarge paragraph 28, please. Thanks. Also in the Macedonian so the witness ...

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In page 5934, you were asked about the adoption of military standards and procedures within your brigade and you were read a sentence from paragraph 28 from the statement of Mr. Gezim Ostreni. In particular, "because of the short period between March 2001, when I joined the NLA, and early August, when the Ohrid Agreement was signed, it was impossible to adopt all planned military standards and procedures." What would you consider this plan, military standards and procedures, that Mr. Ostreni is referring?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the implementation of the rules, certainly, certainly during the -- during the implementation of the rules, from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly he was saying that from the beginning to the end it was impossible to achieve, to implement all the regulations. That's what you are stating.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even though it was the beginning of July, rather late, the formation of Brigade 114 we didn't manage to set up all the structures in the context of Brigade 114 but we did set up most of them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we hear constant noise.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour and actually my computer apparently made the screen disappear, sorry. If I can ... I cannot see the transcript, basically. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll attempt to secure a technician to help, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to look at another screen in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yeah, I will manage to look at the other one. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, could we please display 65 ter 1D823 and if we could go to page 1D00-7210. If we could go to the second page, please. And focus in paragraph (b).

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you just testified that in free time it was not necessarily required to wear uniforms. Therefore, if a soldier was not engaged in any combat activity, was it required to wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you clarify, what is true, that if he is not engaged in combat activities he doesn't have -- is not required to wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. If he was in his free time, they were not obliged to wear uniforms. But when they were in an action, or in the course of duty, at the point they were supposed to be stationed, then they should wear uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, you were shown by my learned colleague this document and in particular he read to you paragraph (b), where it says that on the 6th of March, 2001, alleged members of the NLA were not wearing uniform when withdrawing from Tanushevc. Is this particular case, this example -- is this particular case an example where uniforms would not be required?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we would object on a preliminary basis the witness has not given any evidence that he knew of that particular incident. I would also indicate for the record that the -- this document was refused admission when we used it. But the most important matter in this connection is if Ms. Regue intends to ask the witness whether he can give any evidence as to whether this particular case of record of members of the NLA not wearing any uniform is an indication of members of the NLA being on vacation or out of duty. He should be asked whether he knows of the incident in question. From the answers which were given by the witness during my questioning or the questioning by the Defence it would seem that it didn't, but I believe it would have to be ascertained in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- focus on this particular case, my question was, in general when a NLA soldier was withdrawing from its position, if that was an example of combat operation in that particular case he was required to wear uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you wait, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, when members of the NLA were withdrawing from positions that they were occupying, is this an example where uniform is not required to be worn?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During the withdrawal from the position they had to wear uniforms. Only during their free time they may not be wearing uniform, if they didn't wish to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, when they are withdrawing from a position, are they engaged in any sort of military action?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which circumstances?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there are war circumstances, then the withdrawal is done in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. You were also shown the video depicting the photo of Commander Teli. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And you testified that he was caught out of action when he was killed. What did you mean with that? This is in page 5943, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to interrupt again but I remember the evidence of the witness to have been that Mr. Teli had been sent to Skopje for the purpose of doing reconnaissance, and this would indicate that he was actually on active duty at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can explore this issue further if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Teli was sent to Skopje -- you testified he was sent to Skopje in an observation and reconnaissance mission. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah, you could call that Mr. Teli was in a reconnaitre mission. At the moment he was killed he was resting; he was actually sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Taking your question, would you say that when a person is resting -- when a person is sleeping, is he required to wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. You were also shown today several photos, exhibits 2D54, to exhibits 2D67. Do you recall these photos that my learned colleague Mr. Apostolski showed to you today?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I would like to make a comment on the last photo, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please answer my questions first, Mr. Bushi. I would like to know whether the people that you saw in these photos were actively engaged in military operations when these photos were taken?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the moment when the photo was taken. Some of them were active in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So in case -- but my question was, Mr. Bushi, whether these photos that you testified that they were taken when the -- probably during the mobilisation of some of the soldiers. They were actually in action, in the field, fighting?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that they were fighting. It may be during a war period but not necessarily fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So let's distinguish these two points. They were in the war period but in the photos were they participating -- were they actually fighting in any combat?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. They were not fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go back to Mr. Ostreni's statement, which is 65 ter 2D00-367, page number 6. And if we can enlarge paragraph 28. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You were read in page 5939, paragraph 28 of Mr. Ostreni's statement. I'm going to read it aloud to you again: "From the beginning, the functional and disciplinary authority in the NLA was not determined by the rank system but by the hierarchy of positions. Therefore, in the NLA it was common when addressing a senior member, to address him with a functional position like brigade commander, rather with the rank corresponding to this position." Mr. Bushi, when you had -- when you had the position of brigade commander and you had the rank of colonel, were you the person in the 114th Brigade who had both the highest rank and also the highest position in the hierarchy of the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was this the case in the other brigades?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would you agree that establishing a system of ranks would take some time, meaning producing sufficient number of ranks and deliver them to the field was not one thing, one matter which could be done in a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these things cannot happen overnight.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
