utterances.text: Would you agree that the NLA progressively during 2001 introduced the ranks within its brigades?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was something that was done progressively.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour simply to indicate that we believe if the Prosecution were to seek to rely on this evidence as a matter relevant to their case, the time-period during which the Prosecution claims those ranks were introduced should be specified, we believe, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Actually, I'm trying to find out that from the evidence from the witness which was the time-period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed with that inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you aware, if you are aware, how long -- how it should take in order to establish this system of ranks, considering that you joined the NLA in July 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It lasted until it was disbanded. I stated even earlier we knew when we started it, but we didn't know when it was going to end.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe you didn't understand my question, Mr. Bushi. Just let me start. When you joined the NLA in the 1st of July, 2001, did you have in your brigade a full system of ranks established?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July, not all. This was something that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I think that I addressed Mr. Mettraux's concern, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In page 5937, you testified that you detained members of your brigade after they had failed to comply with internal rules of the NLA. Do you recall giving this evidence, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which actions did you take, which procedure did you follow after these persons were detained?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may not be so important, but I think the question should be asked correctly. The evidence at 5937 was that it was one person singular, not persons that was subjected to any such disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is right, is it Ms. Regue?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Actually the question that was asked, it was in singular: Do you recall whether the military police in your brigade had ever detained someone, a member of your brigade, for not observing the discipline? Yes. So he was asking in the singular, Your Honour. So if you wish I can inquire whether they actually detained or arrested more people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you want to find out whether only one person was arrested or more?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, did you detain one or more members of your brigade for failing to comply with internal rules?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more than one.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you recall the approximate number, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, I cannot give an accurate number because when they were detained they were kept for one or two days. I would say maximum ten persons, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You just said that they were kept for one or two days. So after you detained them and you -- and you kept them, what would you do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that small detention, let's say, we -- an officer talked to them and the commander was one -- Commander Xhaviti was one of such officers who went to meet them, to talk with them, to advise them not do such things, to improve their behaviour. Things like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please display 65 ter 1D905, page number 5. Yeah, if we could -- if we could go to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, in pages 5867 and also in pages 5936, you were asked about this statement that you made during proofing. These are the proofing notes, Your Honours. In particular, with regards to the paragraph which reads -- I will read it to you because it is only in English: "It took two to three days to form the 114th Brigade. It did not take long to form the brigade because the 114th was an extension of the 113th which was already in existence. New members and some of the members of the 113th were taken to form the 114th." In response to my colleague's question you answer: "That it took two to three days to set up the staff, but mobilisation and establishment of the brigade continued until the end, until demobilisation." Could you please explain what did you mean when you were drawing this distinction between the setting up of the staff and mobilisation and establishment of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of the brigade staff is done according to the formation to fill in these formations with the number available to us. As for mobilisation of the brigade, it carried on till the demobilisation of the NLA, till the 26th of September because, at that time, we didn't know when the war would end. If the Ohrid Agreement was not signed, the mobilisation would have continued beyond the 26th. This was a voluntary army, and we didn't have a designated number, 2.000 or 3.000 soldiers. Everyone who came to join, they became soldiers of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call again 65 ter 2D00-367, page 11. It is Mr. Ostreni's statement again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In pages 5931 until 5933, you were asked about coordinate operations with other brigades and you testified that you only had coordination activities with the 113th Brigade as far as the front line is concerned. Furthermore, you were also asked whether each brigade worked in coordination with the General Staff and you answer in the positive. Then you were read paragraph 53 of Mr. Ostreni's statement. In particular, you were read: "Every brigade had an area, zone of responsibility, and each was fighting according to its own plan and judgement. We actually did not have a chance to conduct any coordinate operations involving several brigades because the cease-fire agreement was in force from 6 July and we respected it." After being read this extract of Mr. Ostreni, you were confronted that your evidence and Ostreni's evidence was contradictory. Would you agree that the statement, this paragraph is talking about coordinate activities between brigades?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that the interpretation of the statement given by someone else should be left to that someone else when he comes to testify or to the Judges to the extent that the paragraph in question could be put to the Judges. I don't think it is for the witness to interpret the purported statement of another witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness was confronted with these -- exactly with this two, three lines and it was put to him that it was in contradiction. I just wanted to explore whether he believes that this is in contradiction with what he has stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is a proper subject for re-examination, Ms. Regue. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you want me to ask you again, or did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question. No need to repeat yourself. My statement is not contradictory to his statement. It depends on how people understand it. When I said coordination between brigades it was not coordination of action but coordination as far as the front line is concerned, because we shared the same front line. And all our actions were carried out pursuant to the planning and to the immediate judgment, assessment of the situation. There were specific cases when we had to coordinate with General Gezim Ostreni but these were not everyday cases. These were special cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. About this coordination, about this dialogue with Mr. Gezim Ostreni, was -- would that dialogue take place during your daily briefings?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When it would take place then? I'm referring actually about your daily communication with Mr. Gezim Ostreni, if you were discussing these issues during your daily communication with Mr. Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Gezim Ostreni during our everyday communications we would inform him about the situation in the terrain, about the activities carried out by us until that moment and about future activities, what we planned to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: From the side of Mr. Ostreni, what he would tell you during these daily communications?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the information we provided him with. He would add something as far as the activities of the brigade were concerned, and the tasks received from General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So basically he will issue orders, tasks? Can I take that from your answer?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence will ask that this question and the evidence which was given by the witness either be redacted or given no weight, Your Honour. This was not the evidence of the witness; it was evidence given by counsel. The second issue, Your Honour, is we really believe that to the extent that the Prosecution believed those issues to be relevant to its case, in fairness it should have been put in examination-in-chief not in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was actually put in examination-in-chief and this witness testified about his daily briefings with Mr. Gezim Ostreni through satellite phones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in re-examination what is the issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was just trying to -- I was just trying to, Your Honours, to draw the distinction between an alleged contradiction that my learned colleague put to the witness which we believe that it was in existence because two different matters were actually put on the table to

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Coordination between brigades and communication or coordination with General Staff. That's why it was [Indiscernible] in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would appear, Mr. Mettraux, that there is a sound enough basis for the course of re-examination on this point. By making that observation, we say nothing about what weight we will attach to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we have displayed, please, Exhibit P321. And if we can go to page bearing ERN R037-6858.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, that -- that you were shown during cross-examination this document?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In pages 5871 until 5874, you made some comments with regards to this page and also to the following pages. In particular, you testified that 117th and -- you made some comments in particular with regards to 111th and 114th. Do you recall making those comments?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 114th existed. The Fadin Imani, Tigri Brigade, based in Nikustak while 111th Brigade was at a state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I meant 111th and 117th, not 14th.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 111st was a brigade in a state of readiness, whilst 117th -- I did not know that such a thing existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to see in the chart that actually these two brigades are depicted with intermittent lines. Are you able to see that in the photo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Aside from these corrections, Mr. Bushi, is this structure correct, adequate in the meaning that the brigades are reporting up to the General Staff and the General Staff is ordering down to the brigades?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, being shown this chart as well?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Bushi, you testified that your political leader was Ali Ahmeti. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see Ali Ahmeti in the higher-up of this structure?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You also testified that Ali Ahmeti had a close group of people working with him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Despite the corrections that you made with regards to three names, I believe, would you agree that the structure reflects this general situation, with regards to the political leadership of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names here, yes; but it is possible that there were other names as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall being shown this chart in cross-examination, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall correcting some names mentioned in this chart?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have a military leadership or military command which had in the higher up Mr. Ostreni and Mr. Ahmeti, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sure. Within the military leadership, who were the people who were in the higher positions of the military leadership of the NLA, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmeti and the General Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Does this chart reflect these facts that both of these people were at the higher top -- at the top positions of the structure?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could we inquire, Ms. Regue, whether you are about to finish or whether it would be preferable to have a break at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This is actually one more page with regards to these documents so if we can wrap up this subject matter it would be more convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing this chart, Mr. Bushi, during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall introducing changes with regards to the names of some of the brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, did I change the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I think that you clarified the names of the brigade commanders of the 112th and the 113th and also your first name, with regards to the 114th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But you agree with the names of the brigade commanders, the remaining brigade commanders. Do you recall that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they look now, they weren't those, but with the changes that I made, those remained until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, so that the question perhaps is put more precisely to the witness, he has also indicated that he did not know two of the purported brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bushi, do you see in the higher up of this structure Mr. Gezim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was he the person that the brigade commanders were reporting to and the person who was issuing the orders to the brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Does the chart reflects this general structure, this structure?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a diagram, yes; but not with the names on it now. With the corrections that I made, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Including the corrections that you made, the diagram, the structure is an accurate description of the way that the NLA was working?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at a quarter past. It would appear that it is not going to be feasible to commence the next witness in the remaining time today from what we judge to be the progress. I indicate that in case, Mr. Saxon, it may be possible to give some indication to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Could we please called Exhibit P462.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you were asked, I believe yesterday in page 5955 whether you had any city under your control and you responded in the negative. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You indicated in your evidence in chief that your headquarters were in the village of Nikustak which I believe is indicated with number 4 in this map. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was your brigade present and operating in this village, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You also indicated with number 5 that the headquarters of the 1st Battalion included Nagustak village and Vistica, and I believe that you indicated that with number 5. Was your brigade present and operating in this area in Nagustak and Vistica?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vistica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You then indicated -- you drew a circle indicating the operational area of your brigade which, if I'm not mistaken, ran from Vistica, Nagustak, Bara, and Zara [phoen]. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was your brigade operating in this area?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it operated in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove, actually, this photo and if we could have, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if my colleague could, as far as these villages that she mentioned are concerned, clarify whether they're villages or towns, because her previous question was whether they had under their control a town, a city, so I think that she should clarify with this witness for which inhabited area her question is about, whether a village or a town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That can be a lovely factual question, Mr. Apostolski, and divide a city from a town, and a town from a village. But we'll see how far Ms. Regue is able to explore that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, how would you define these villages or towns that you mentioned, villages or towns?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could have please MFI 1D229, page 7. If we could ... I believe this is not the right page. It should be page 7. If you -- of the document. If you could go two more pages. Yeah, this is the page. And if we could scroll down, please, and zoom in the last paragraph, according to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, Defence counsel read to you an extract of this document, in particular this last paragraph which says that: "According to the available but as yet unconfirmed information, the 114th Brigade is said to have received the order to close the existing gap north of Skopje between Radusa and Tanusevci. This would, therefore, make possible fighting in the whole area of the 111th [Realtime transcript read in error "11th"], 113th and 114th." You testified in 5648 that was a pending order depending on the successful signing of the Ohrid Agreement. I'd like to ask you, was the 111th Brigade operational in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't operational at any point in time. From the beginning and up to the end of the war it wasn't operational; it was in a state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Upon which conditions, if you have knowledge about that, the 111th Brigade would have become operational?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in case the Ohrid Agreement was not signed. In that case, it would have started its operations in its area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can we have please 65 ter 1D761, page number 3. And just for the transcript in page 59, line 23, it is 11th and it should read 111th.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall that my learned colleagues read to you some extracts from different statements?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we look at --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Actually, I think that the Macedonian should be the page before this one. Only the Macedonian -- and scroll down. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We see in paragraph 4 that this document which actually is the witness's statement of Xhezair Shaqiri. It reads that: "I came to the area of Ljuboten, Sunday, 12th August." Now in paragraph 5, and I believe that we should move to the next page in the Macedonian version. The first line of paragraph 5 reads: "It was very difficult to withdraw at that moment without any victims." If we go two lines below it says: "I then order the commanders to begin withdrawal." Then if we could go to the next page, next page only in English, paragraph 6. The first line reads: "There are no facts that NLA were present in Ljuboten. The fact is that Ljube Boskoski was there." I'd like you to listen to my question carefully, Mr. Bushi. Would you agree that in this statement Mr. Xhezair Shaqiri and the rest of the soldiers never reach Ljuboten on the 12th of August? I'm just asking to you comment on what this document reads.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What Xhezair Shaqiri said in his statement means that there was no order issued by me as brigade commander to enter Ljuboten and that this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, did you read, did you see in this extract that Xhezair Shaqiri or any member of the NLA ever reach Ljuboten on the 12th of August. I'm not talking about your orders. I'm just talking about fact whether any NLA member enter Ljuboten that day.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't reach at all. They didn't set out and they did not reach the village because they couldn't go.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you read also, did you see in this document whether there was any indication that NLA soldiers were present in Ljuboten on the 12th or even prior to the 12th?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 1D507, also page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We see that the last line of paragraph 8 - this is Suad Saliu's statement - reads: "We were trying to get closer to Ljuboten but we were prevented by Macedonian direct fire." Just looking at this extract, Mr. Bushi, would you agree that this person states that they never reached Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 1D94. And page 4, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In paragraph 17, -- this is the witness's statement of Islam Zendeli. In paragraph 17 we can read in the first line: "We walked through the woods towards Ljuboten. Two lines below it says: "The Macedonian forces notice us and they started to shell at us." Paragraph 18 it reads: "At some stage after two or three hours or maybe a bit more, we got an order that we should withdraw and that's what we did." Paragraph 19, the last line, I believe that we should go to the next page in the Macedonian version. Paragraph 19, the last line reads: "As far as I know, there were no members of the NLA in the village when it was attacked." Also, from what you listen, Mr. Bushi, did Islam Zendeli or any other members of the NLA ever reach Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. And they did not set out.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would you agree that in this statement there is no indication at that there was no NLA presence on the 12th or prior to the 12th, 2001 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that there is no indication of NLA presence there on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit P215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for clarification purposes, Your Honour, was counsel asking about the entire statement or was she asking simply about the one sentence that was read, because in fact the statement suggests, or seems to suggest otherwise, Your Honour; namely, that there were members of the NLA around or in the surroundings of the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question was about the village itself not about the surroundings of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's as I understood it, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit P215. This is the witness's statement of protected Witness M-092 and, sorry, I didn't locate the page. It should be paragraph 33, which is in page 8; I apologise. The next page then.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thanks for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just ensuring that it isn't displayed on any public display.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: My fault. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It should be the next page in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Paragraph 33, the last five -- excuse me, three lines read: "As I was told, Xhezair Shaqiri on the Sunday afternoon, was with the soldiers above Pop Cesma. When the NLA soldiers were wounded, he ordered them to withdraw to Matejce because he was informed that the Ohrid Agreement was reached." Would you agree from this extract that any NLA soldier ever reach Ljuboten village on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the witness's statement from the screen. And just to wrap up --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, from all the statements that you saw, despite some contradictions, would you agree that they have one thing in common is that none of these statements indicate that NLA ever reach Ljuboten village on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In pages 5766 and 5767, you were asked by my learned colleague about the representation of minorities in the parliament and also in the government and you agree on the percentage put forward by my colleague, but you testified that it was a matter of equal representation in the Macedonian institutions. If we could please go to the Ohrid Agreement, which is Exhibit P84 P34 and start with page 9, please. Yeah, if we could scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you what it says, the last paragraph of page 9. "Taking into account the recommendations of the already established government commission, the parties will take concrete action to increase the representation of members of communities not in the majority in Macedonia in public administration, the military, and public enterprises as well as to improve their access to public financing for business development." Mr. Bushi, do you remember that you were also shown Exhibit 1D119, that is in page 5819, where it was actually Ministry of Interior report dating 24th of April, 2001, about a meeting held in order to discuss the training of some 500 newly recruited police officers. Do you recall being shown this document by my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And my learned colleague also put to that you actually the Macedonian state had started back in April to increase the number of ethnic Albanians in public employment and he show you this document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lawyer said so, but this was not accurate because that started after the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to the last page of the Ohrid Agreement, please. Yeah, we are there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 5.2 reads: "The parties commit themselves to ensuring that the police services will by 2004 generally reflect the composition and distribution of the population of Macedonia. As initial steps toward this end, the parties commit to ensure that 500 new police officers from communities not in the majority in the population of Macedonia will be hired and trained by July 2002, and that these officers will be deployed to the areas where such communities live." Does the Ohrid Agreement foresees the implementation of measures to increase the participation of minorities within the public institutions of Macedonia, including the police force?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it foresees that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Also, in pages 5912 to 5913 you were asked by my learned colleague that the constitution guaranteed the cohabitation of Macedonian people of different ethnicities and you were read the preamble. Do you recall that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was preamble number 7, if I remember right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, you were actually read the preamble, and then you were read Article number 7, and you actually testified that they were changed after the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to pages 3 of the Ohrid Agreement that we have now on the screen, please, page number 3. I think, yeah, if we could scroll down, please. And also in the Macedonian. I believe that it should be the next page in the Macedonian version. My apologies. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you see -- can you see, Mr. Bushi, in item number 9 of the Ohrid Agreement it says: "Annexes. The following annexes constitute integral parts of this Framework Agreement, and we see, (a), constitutional amendments; (b), legislative modifications. And then if we go a bit down in the document we see Annex A. My apologies?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see it in Macedonian. It's not before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In Macedonian it should be ERN N000-9982. If you could go down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see in the item number 9 annexes and then: "The following annexes constitute integral parts of this Framework Agreement, and we see, (a), constitutional amendments; (b), legislative modifications." Do you see that, Mr. Bushi, now?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And then, I believe, in the Macedonian version we have to move to the next page. It says: "Annex (a), constitutional amendments," and then the preamble and there is a new drafting of the preamble. And then if we could change to the next page in English. Do you also see, Mr. Bushi, that the Article 7, the Article 7 that was read to you was also modified in the Ohrid Agreement? In the Macedonian version, it is in the bottom part of the screen.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just wondering if it is a convenient time because I'm going move to another issue.

utterances.text: Very well. In the circumstances, it is necessary that we again adjourn for the day to resume tomorrow at 9.00.
